blocks.html: Robinsons Land Corporation (RLC) officially renamed Bridgetowne Boulevard as John Gokongwei Jr. Boulevard on August 5, 2026, creating a permanent tribute to the founder of the Gokongwei Group, whose values continue to guide the company today.

The ceremony takes place a few days before what would have been Mr. John’s 100th birthday on August 11. By naming the road in his honor, RLC celebrates a century of his vision while recognizing the hard work, resilience, discipline, prudence, and long-term thinking that shaped his life and the businesses he built.

The location gives the homage particular meaning. John Gokongwei Jr. Boulevard stretches approximately one kilometer through Bridgetowne Destination Estate, one of RLC’s most significant mixed-use developments, spanning portions of Quezon City and Pasig.
Mr. John was a young boy of 13 when his father died. As the eldest child, he began helping support the family and learned at an early age to meet hardship with resourcefulness.

Those experiences influenced the way he later approached business. He studied what customers needed, managed resources carefully, and pursued innovative ideas that could create lasting value. From those beginnings, he established enterprises that brought products, services, jobs, and new possibilities to millions of Filipinos.

Through Robinsons Land, that people-first outlook took physical form. Robinsons Galleria was an early expression of the company’s mixed-use approach, bringing commercial, office, residential, and hospitality spaces together in one complex. The idea was not simply to put different buildings side by side, but to create a destination shaped around the varied needs of everyday life.
That approach later guided RLC’s expansion into new communities and emerging areas, supported by disciplined development, careful stewardship, and a long-term view.
A Road That Carries the Vision Forward

Bridgetowne brings the mixed-use concept first pursued at Robinsons Galleria to a grander scale. The estate combines workplaces, homes, retail, hospitality, leisure facilities, and public spaces within one destination.

Running through its center, John Gokongwei Jr. Boulevard plays an essential role in making that vision work. Along the road is a 200-meter bridge that provides a direct route between the Quezon City and Pasig City sides of Bridgetowne.

Bridgetowne can be reached through C-5 Road, Ortigas Avenue, and Amang Rodriguez Avenue. Together, these routes improve mobility for residents, employees, businesses, and visitors while strengthening the estate’s links to surrounding communities.

The boulevard’s practical purpose makes it especially meaningful as a tribute to Mr. John. Throughout his life, he built businesses around the needs of Filipinos and broadened access to products, travel, education, and employment. At Bridgetowne, that same people-first philosophy is reflected in a road designed to make daily movement easier and support the communities it connects.
With the renaming, his name becomes part of a place shaped by the same belief that guided his life’s work: growth is most meaningful when it improves lives and strengthens communities.
